units.title: The Safe Workbench
units.blurb: Low voltage only, batteries and soldering done the careful way.

units.title: Circuits on a Breadboard
units.blurb: Ohm's law, the resistor every LED needs, and voltage dividers.

units.title: Talking to a Microcontroller

topics.title: A Safe Electronics Bench
topics.short: Low-voltage kits, batteries handled by the maker's rules, and a soldering iron that always goes back in its stand.
topics.trouble: Beginners treat a lithium battery like an AA cell, or set a hot iron down on the table.

topics.title: Ohm's Law on a Breadboard
topics.short: Voltage pushes, resistance resists, and current is the result: V = IR.
topics.trouble: Students mix up milliamps and amps, or forget which breadboard holes are connected.

topics.title: The Resistor Every LED Needs
topics.short: Pick the series resistor from what is left after the LED's forward voltage: R = (V - Vf)/I.
topics.trouble: Students divide the whole supply voltage by the current, forgetting the LED's own voltage drop.

topics.title: Voltage Dividers and Sensors
topics.short: Two resistors in series split a voltage; a light sensor in a divider turns light into volts.
topics.trouble: Students put the wrong resistor on top of the fraction, R1 instead of the one between the output and ground.

topics.title: Analog Readings
topics.short: An analog-to-digital converter turns 0 to 3.3 V into a whole number from 0 to 1023 (10-bit) or 4095 (12-bit).
topics.trouble: Students use 1024 or 4096 as the top reading instead of one less.

topics.title: PWM: Fast Switching for Motors and Lights
topics.short: Switch fully on and off very fast; the fraction of time on, the duty cycle, sets the average voltage.
topics.trouble: Students think PWM makes a lower steady voltage, or confuse the frequency with the duty cycle.
